4-PORTS 10/100/1000M GIGABIT INDUSTRIAL PoE+ EXTENDER USER MANUAL
1. Package Contents
Thank you for purchasing FS Industrial 1-Port 802.3bt PoE++ to 4-Port 802.3af/at Gigabit PoE Extender, IPOEX4. In the following sections,
the term “Industrial PoE Extender” means the IPOEX4.
Open the box of the IPOEX4 and carefully unpack it. The box should contain the following items:
l Industrial PoE Extender x 1
l User’s Manual x 1
l RJ45 Dust Cap x 5
l Wall Mounting Kit x 1
If any of these are missing or damaged, please contact your dealer immediately; if possible, retain the carton including the original
packing material, and use them again to repack the product in case there is a need to return it to us for repair.
2. Hardware Introduction
This section describes the functionalities of the Industrial PoE Extender’s components.
2.1 Front Panel
Figure 2-1 shows the front panel of Industrial PoE Extender.

3. Installation
This section describes the functionalities of the Industrial PoE Extender’s components and guides you to installing it on the DIN rail and
wall. Please read this chapter completely before continuing.
Note:
This following pictures show how to install the device. However, the device in the picture is not the IPOEX4.
3.1 DIN-rail Mounting Installation
3.2 Wall-mount Plate Mounting
3.3 Connecting IPOEX4 to PSE
The Industrial PoE Extender has five RJ45 ports of which one is the PoE++ In port connected to the PSE and the other four are PoE+
Out ports connected to the PDs.
Step 1: Connect a standard Cat5e/6 UTP cable from a remote PSE, such as PoE switch, to the “PoE++ In” port of the IPOEX4.
3

[p6]
4-PORTS 10/100/1000M GIGABIT INDUSTRIAL PoE+ EXTENDER USER MANUAL
Step 2: The PSE delivers both Ethernet Data and PoE power over UTP cable to the IPOEX4 and the “PoE IN” LED will be lit steadily.
Note:
1. When the LED turns steady green, it means the IPOEX4 is being powered successfully with PoE.
2.If the LED is not lit, please check the remote PSE or the cable connecting to a PC or a network device to see if the cable is correct.
Or with an 802.3at device such as the target PD, check whether the power injection is correct.
3. Never connect any non-standard PoE PSE to the IPOEX4; it will damage the device permanently.
4. Refer to Chapter 2.2 for more information about LED function.
3.4 Connecting IPOEX4 to PD
Step 1: Connect the additional Cat5e/6 cable from the PoE+ Out of the IPOEX4 to a remote PD.
4

[p7]
4-PORTS 10/100/1000M GIGABIT INDUSTRIAL PoE+ EXTENDER USER MANUAL
Step 2: The PoE+ Out port is also the power injector, which transmits DC voltage to the Cat5e/6 cable and transfers data and power
simultaneously between the PSE and PD.
Step 3: Once the IPOEX4 detects the existence of an IEEE 802.3at/af device, the PoE-in-Use LED indicator will be lit steadily, showing
it is providing power.
5
3

[p8]
4-PORTS 10/100/1000M GIGABIT INDUSTRIAL PoE+ EXTENDER USER MANUAL
Note:
1.If the connected device is not fully complying with IEEE 802.3af/at standard or in-line power device, the PoE-in-Use LED indicator
of the IPOEX4 will not be lit steadily.
2. According to IEEE 802.3af/at standard, the IPOEX4 will not inject power to the cable if not connecting to a standard IEEE 802.3af/at
device.
3. DO NOT connect any PSE to port 1~ port 4 of the IPOEX4; it may damage the device permanently.
4. Power over Ethernet Budget
The following table lists how many PoE devices can be powered by the IPOEX4 under 1m distance:
Power Source PoE Output Budget* Max. Number of PDs supported
Class 4 PD@25 watts 3 units
95W PoH PSE 75 watts max. Class 3 PD@12.9 watts 4 units
Class 2 PD@7 watts 4 units
Class 4 PD@25 watts 3 units
90W 802.3bt PoE++ Type 4
75 watts max. Class 3 PD@12.9 watts 4 units
PSE
Class 2 PD@7 watts 4 units
Class 4 PD@25 watts 2 units
60W 802.3bt PoE++ Type 3
50 watts max. Class 3 PD@12.9 watts 3 units
PSE
Class 2 PD@7 watts 4 units
Class 3 PD@12.9 watts 1 units
30W 802.3at PoE+ PSE 25 watts max.
Class 2 PD@7 watts 3 units
Remark:
1. The PoE output budget means the aggregated power output of the 4 PSE ports.
2. The aggregated power consumption will be below 60 watts if with PoE+ PSE.
3. Please check the power input LED for optimal power output.
6
